item.title: AWS-DFD-Visualizer - v2.7.2 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

# AWS-DFD-Visualizer v2.7.2 Release Notes

## 🌟 Enhancements & Security Integration

* **Hybrid Dynamic JIT SPL Drilldowns ([Issue #2](https://github.com/JohnYoungSuh/AWS-DFD-Visualizer/issues/2))**: Implemented secure token escaping (`sanitizeSplunkToken`) and query interpolation in node/link click handlers. Allows users to click visualizer elements to instantly search VPC flow logs or configuration history.

* **Tenable/Nessus & Threat Telemetry Overlays**:

- Implemented flashing red keyframe pulsing styling on compute node cards flagged with threat alert statuses (`status\="incident"`, `status\="failing"`).

- Added vulnerability status overrides that map critical CVE scan findings (`status\="Critical"`) to a custom **"skull"** icon.

- Shipped predefined search macros in `default/macros.conf` to easily join Nessus, GuardDuty, or latency events with `aws:config` topology data.

* **Native Print & SVG Export Controls**:

- Added a client-side "Download SVG/PNG" button using SVG serialization to allow raw diagram downloads, bypassing Splunk's headless PDF clipping issues.

- Established print-friendly media CSS overrides (`@media print`).

* **Visual and Contrast Adjustments**:

- **Dynamic Theme Contrast ([Issue #4](https://github.com/JohnYoungSuh/AWS-DFD-Visualizer/issues/4))**: VPC, Subnet, and Plane labels adapt font colors dynamically based on light/dark mode.

- **Compliance Edge Violation Styling ([Issue #5](https://github.com/JohnYoungSuh/AWS-DFD-Visualizer/issues/5))**: Violated paths (e.g., SSH/22 SG violations) render as dashed bold red lines with warning icons. VPC/Subnet headers display active violation counts.

- **Resource Lifecycle Decorator ([Issue #6](https://github.com/JohnYoungSuh/AWS-DFD-Visualizer/issues/6))**: Deleted assets (`configurationItemStatus: ResourceDeleted`) render with a strikethrough, and stale configuration items fade out dynamically.

- **Hover Halos & Zoom LOD ([Issue #7](https://github.com/JohnYoungSuh/AWS-DFD-Visualizer/issues/7))**: Hovering on nodes scales labels and adds a high-contrast text shadow/halo. SVG zooms trigger LOD adjustments (hiding text/shadows at $k \< 0.45$) to save rendering performance.

* **Identity Plane Spacing**: Increased the horizontal spacing gap parameter for unassociated Identity plane nodes to prevent AssumesRole link labels from overlapping.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

* **Static Grouped Layout Spacing and Centering**: Resolved visual overlaps in the static grouped hierarchy layout ("Blueprint Mode") by replacing the fixed-size `treeLayout.size` with dynamic `treeLayout.nodeSize` coordinates mapping and coordinate shifting/centering bounds calculations.

* **Clamped Coordinate Scaling & Dynamic viewBox Width**: Prevented card overlaps in wide tree layouts by clamping the coordinate compression factor (`scaleX` / `scaleY`) to a minimum safe threshold. Implemented dynamic `viewBox` width/height expansion to automatically fit the expanded clamped tree.

* **Overlapping Parallel Edges**: Aggregated bidirectional edge records with multiple connecting protocols into a single visual edge with a comma-separated label.

* **Case-Sensitivity Option Parser**: Resolved a configuration parsing bug where `clusterBy` and `layoutMode` values failed to parse unless written in exact lowercase format.

* **Release Hygiene Sync**: Version synchronized to `2.7.2` across `package.json`, `splunk-app-manifest.json`, `Makefile`, `default/app.conf`, and UI header.

---

## 📍 GitHub Issues Status

The GitHub issues list **has not been updated yet**.

The following 6 resolved issues are still marked as **Open** on GitHub:

1. **#8** `docs: Upgrade Application Screenshots`

2. **#7** `style: Hover State Font Enlargement and Background Halo`

3. **#6** `style: Resource Lifecycle & Staleness Text Styling`

4. **#5** `style: Compliance Violation Styling for Edge & Zone Labels`

5. **#4** `style: Dynamic Contrast Text Labels for Planes, VPC, and Subnet`

6. **#2** `feat: Hybrid Dynamic JIT Drilldown SPL Generation`


Short Description:
Interactive AWS Data Flow Diagrams (DFD) for Splunk. Visualizes AWS Config topologies, nested VPCs/Subnets, and Zero-Trust compliance highlights.


Description:
AWS DFD Visualizer (Splunkbase App Summary) Purpose & Background Auditing complex cloud infrastructure for compliance (e.g., DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5), NIST 800-53, or NIST 800-207 Zero-Trust Architectures) is extremely challenging. While AWS accounts generate high-volume telemetry from AWS Config, VPC Flow Logs, and GuardDuty, reviewing these complex configurations in standard tabular logs or flat Splunk tables makes it difficult for security teams, system auditors, and DevSecOps engineers to analyze isolation boundaries, spot structural gaps, or verify access routes. The Solution The AWS DFD (Data Flow Diagram) Visualizer solves this by transforming raw relationship logs and configuration items into interactive, visual security topologies styled after AWS Application Composer. It gives compliance officers and analysts an intuitive, visual framework to audit security posture in real-time. Key Features: Zero-Trust Layout Engine: Segregates assets deterministically into distinct swimlanes—separating the Identity plane (users/roles), Policy & Control plane (global network assets like WAF/CloudFront), and Infrastructure plane (VPCs/Subnets). Nested Enclosures: Renders nested container boundaries representing VPCs and Subnets with real-time compliance validation markers. Security & Telemetry Overlays: Highlights Security Group associations as outer compliance rings around compute nodes (Green for compliant, Red for non-compliant). Automatically isolates and flashes incident-flagged resources in pulsing red alerts. Overrides critical Nessus/Tenable vulnerability states with a custom "skull" threat icon. Dynamically intercepts and highlights non-compliant connection paths (e.g., SSH/22 path violations) as dashed Vibrant Red links. Dashboard Studio & SimpleXML Ready: Integrates natively with Splunk Dashboard Studio, supporting dynamic click-capturing drilldown tokens, responsive light/dark themes, and performance-saving Level of Detail (LOD) controls. Export & Live Console Feed: Includes a native client-side SVG/PNG exporter, a standard draw.io XML generator, and an ad-hoc CSV console feed for drafting cloud topologies on the fly. 🛠️ Configuration & Code Updates Done: To align your app bundle with this new description, I have updated the description strings in the following files: package.json splunk-app-manifest.json default/app.conf Additionally: Added /cypress/screenshots/ to .gitignore to keep the repository clean of test artifacts. Ran npm run build to compile the production bundle (webpack compiled successfully). Committed the changes and successfully pushed them to master.

item.title: WithSecure Elements Add-on - v1.0.3 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Daemon-style polling

Both modular inputs (withsecure_epp_input, withsecure_bcd_input) now run as long-lived daemons: each one polls the WithSecure API, sleeps for the configured interval, and repeats — no longer relying on Splunk's modular-input scheduler to relaunch the script after exit. This is the pattern used by solnlib and by the Splunk-published add-ons (AWS, Office 365, Crowdstrike, etc.). It makes periodic polling robust against environments where the scheduler does not reliably relaunch on interval.

Two layers of exception handling keep the daemon alive:

  • inner try/except around _process_input — transient per-input errors (API down, rate limit, network blip) do not break the cycle
  • outer try/except around the loop body — any other unexpected exception is logged and the daemon resumes at the next sleep tick

An INFO heartbeat log is emitted every 10 cycles so operators can see the daemon is healthy even during quiet periods with no new events.

Per-incident KV-store lock

New locks KV-store collection and withsecure_locks.py helper module providing an advisory lock per incident. Both flows that fetch detections — the auto-fetch in the BCD modular input and the on-demand | fetchdetections custom command — acquire the same lock, eliminating the race window where a manual fetch could overlap with a scheduled poll and double-index detections.

  • Atomic acquire via KV-store unique _key constraint
  • 90-second TTL — an expired lock left by a killed process is reclaimed by the next acquirer
  • Auto-fetch input: a denied lock is treated like a transient detection-fetch failure (existing oldest_failed_ts mechanism), so the incident is retried at the next poll
  • | fetchdetections: a denied lock surfaces a WARN message in the Splunk UI ("Auto-fetch is in progress for this incident; showing already-indexed detections only.") and yields the detections already in the index, keeping the analyst's workflow unblocked

Resource impact

item.title: AI Workbench - v1.4.2 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

AI Assistent for Splunk — Release notes

What's new, improved, and fixed in each release, in plain language. This is the
customer-facing summary used for the Splunkbase release-notes section; the
full technical changelog lives in the project's detailed release notes.

Last updated: 2026-06-11

About version numbers. Releases once numbered 0.10–0.13 were renumbered to
1.0–1.3 to reflect production maturity — no behaviour changed. The current
published version is 1.4.2. The 1.5.0 "Data Foundation" features
below are implemented and in final testing; they ship in a later published
build (the version is cut to 1.5.0 once final testing completes).

Next release — 1.5.0 "Data Foundation" (implemented, in final testing)

New

  • Onboard new data sources, not just work with data already in Splunk.
    Describe a source — or attach a sample log file — and the assistant builds a
    deployment-ready set of Splunk add-ons (forwarder inputs, index-time
    parsing, search-time field extractions, CIM tags, and a deployment-server
    mapping) and hands you one downloadable package to push from your own
    deployment server. (Professional and up.)
  • "Is my data actually parsed correctly?" check. The assistant can tell you
    whether a sourcetype has ingestion or timestamp problems — events landing
    at the wrong time, truncated lines, broken line-breaking — by reading Splunk's
    own internal logs for you. It catches feeds that look healthy in TrackMe but
    are mis-onboarded. (Professional and up.)
  • Generated config is validated against your Splunk, and scored. Parsing
    configuration is checked against your instance's own configuration reference
    (no invented settings), and each source gets a 0–100 Data Quality Score
    with an A–F grade across the "Magic 8" onboarding best practices.
  • Attach a local sample file in Ask. Pick a log file from your computer and
    ask for the parsing config — even before the data is in Splunk. Only the file
    name is recorded in the audit trail, never the contents.

Improved

  • More reliable generated dashboards. Help/explanation panels now render as
    formatted HTML instead of showing raw tags; dashboards no longer hit the
    "too many rows" error from an over-fine time-chart interval; CDTSM anomaly
    dashboards respect the model's 24-hour detection-window limit automatically;
    and the AI-Toolkit anomaly/forecast chart always renders as the proper
    visualization     (never falls back to a plain table).
  • Cleaner names for generated objects. Saved searches, models and dashboards
    the assistant creates now use an aiworkbench tag in their names instead of
    aiasst, to avoid confusion with Splunk's own "AI Assistant" app. Objects
    created earlier keep working unchanged.
  • Audit tab improvements. Adds a Business Unit column and a cascading
    Business Unit filter; the User filter is now a dropdown; you can filter
    by whether a request had an attachment; timestamps display in your local
    timezone    ; and the filters are tidied up. Token counts and the request outcome
    now record reliably (a fix to how audit completion events were written) — note
    that, per Splunk's permissions, capturing every user's activity requires the
    Organisation's audit index to be a normal (non-internal) index.

1.4.2

Improved

  • Clearer guidance when a free-tier LLM key runs into its limits. Some
    providers' free tiers are too small for the assistant's requests — for example
    Groq's free tier allows only ~12,000 tokens per minute, which is smaller
    than a typical request, and Google Gemini free-tier keys sometimes return
    a zero quota. The assistant now explains what happened and what to do (upgrade
    the tier, enable billing, or switch providers — or run a local model via
    Ollama) instead of showing the raw provider error, and the LLM configuration
    screen now flags these free-tier limits up front (#8).

Fixed

  • Groq "request too large" (413) and Gemini "quota exceeded … limit: 0" (429)
    errors on even a simple question are now reported with a plain-language fix
    instead of the raw provider message (#8).

1.4.1

New & improved

  • Clearer licensing with edition badges. Tiers are now a simple capability
    matrix — Professional, Enterprise, and MSP editions each show a
    badge in the header, and any feature not in your plan appears with a padlock
    and a short note instead of failing silently. Nothing you have created is
    ever deleted     if your tier changes or a licence lapses — gated features simply
    become unavailable until the tier is restored.

Fixed

  • Turn-level audit logging now records reliably. Browser-side audit events
    (each AI request and response) were not reaching Splunk; they now do.
  • More reliable dashboard generation, including large and HTML-containing
    dashboards.

1.4.0

New

  • The assistant reads your own Splunk, live. It now consults your instance's
    actual search commands and installed visualizations when generating searches
    and dashboards, so the output matches what your environment really supports
    instead of guessing.
  • Splunk Security Essentials integration. Real detection content from SSE is
    available to security templates.

1.3.3

New & improved

  • TrackMe integration, end-to-end. Data feed-health awareness and TrackMe
    actions are wired through and live-verified, alongside richer built-in
    platform knowledge.

1.3.2

  • First Splunkbase 1.x release — packaging and permissions hardening.

1.3.1

Fixed

  • Editing an Organisation or Business Unit could drop some saved fields — fixed.
  • Added a safeguard that keeps the bundled templates correct after upgrades.

1.3.0

New

  • Real audit logging. A defensible, per-Organisation audit trail of every AI
    interaction. (Professional and up.)

1.2.0

New

  • Splunk Security Essentials content tools — templates can reach SSE
    detection content directly.

1.1.1

New

  • Cisco Deep Time Series Model (CDTSM) templates — pre-trained anomaly
    detection and forecasting through the Splunk AI Toolkit, each with a proof
    dashboard.

1.1.0

Improved

  • Multi-tenancy and the Organisation / Business-Unit editor — overhauled for
    clearer, safer tenant scoping.

1.0.0

New

  • Knowledge layer. The assistant can draw on a curated, admin-managed
    knowledge base to ground its answers in your organisation's own conventions.

(Releases before 1.0 are early pre-release history and are omitted here.)

Known issues

  • Open the assistant from inside another app. AI Assistent is a "host shell":
    reach it from a navigation-menu entry inside Search, Enterprise Security, ITSI,
    or your own apps — not by clicking the app tile directly. Everything it creates
    lands in the namespace of the app you opened it from.
  • Some in-development Data Foundation features need self-hosted Splunk. The
    configuration-reference grounding and config-package generation (1.5.0) read
    files on the Splunk server, so they are unavailable on Splunk Cloud; the
    assistant says so and continues with what it can.

When a published fix resolves a tracked GitHub issue, it is summarised here with
its issue number — for example: "Fixed: a dashboard panel could display raw HTML
markup as text instead of formatting it (#123)."


Short Description:
A workbench for Splunk, not just a chatbot. Analyse, correlate and build across SPL, dashboards, alerts, AI Toolkit / MLTK, ES, ITSI and TrackMe through tools that understand each one — plus any MCP server you add. Pick your LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Groq, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenRouter. Multi-tenant, multi-tier (Free, Pro, Enterprise, MSP).


Description:
AI Workbench is a generative workspace for Splunk. Not a chatbot bolted onto search but a real workbench, where you investigate, analyse and build using tools that understand Splunk natively. The Workbench is built as a host shell. It has no use-cases of its own — it derives everything from the Splunk app a user opens it from and the Splunk roles they hold. Install it once on the Search Head, then embed it into the apps your users already live in: Search, ITSI, Enterprise Security, your SOC apps, your MSP customer apps. The same engine renders a different experience per calling app, with different templates, different LLMs, different tools, and writes its outputs into that calling app's namespace. End users never leave the app they came from. Ask in plain English. Get back validated SPL searches, Simple XML dashboards, alerts, lookups, reports and Splunk AI Toolkit (MLTK) pipelines. Every artefact is run for real before it is saved, and every artefact is a normal Splunk knowledge object — owned by the calling user, in the calling app, findable in Splunk's own UI. The depth is the difference. Where a generic MCP-only assistant talks to Splunk through one broad door, AI Workbench ships with fine-grained, Splunk-aware tools across Core, Enterprise Security, ITSI, TrackMe and the AI Toolkit — roughly fifty of them, each scoped to one job a Splunk admin actually does. The LLM picks the right tool for the question, runs it under your existing Splunk ACLs, and shows its work. Extend it further by adding HTTP tools or registering any MCP server in the Tools tab. Two audiences benefit immediately. Splunk users who know what they want but find SPL foreign get production-quality searches and dashboards generated and validated panel-by-panel. Splunk users who bounce off MLTK get an outlier detector, forecaster, classifier or clusterer built end-to-end, with a companion dashboard that proves the model is doing something sensible. Bring your own LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Ollama (local, fully offline) or OpenRouter. Browser-direct for speed, or Splunk-server-side proxy mode so API keys never leave the search head. Bring your own corporate IAM — WebEAM.Next, Ping, Okta, AzureAD, internal SAML — via a customer-supplied Python hook that mints fresh auth headers per request. Multi-tenant by design. Organisations and Business Units are resolved automatically from the calling app and the user's roles — end users don't pick a tenant. Templates, LLM configurations and tool availability all scope per Org or BU. Run one Splunk environment for many teams or many customers without them seeing each other. Tokens and Costs breaks spend down by App, User, Model, Provider, Organisation, BU or LLM configuration — over time, with real per-model pricing. Free, Professional, Enterprise and MSP licence tiers, activated self-serve, air-gap-friendly.

item.title: GenAI Observability for Splunk - v2.0.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Data Model: `GenAI_Traces` (new)

A new event-based data model, GenAI Traces, normalizes GenAI/LLM spans for fast `tstats`-driven dashboards and alerting.

  • Root object `GenAI_Span` constrained to `index=genai_traces` across both `genai:trace` and `genai:otel` sourcetypes, so native SDK traces and OpenTelemetry spans land in one model.
  • 20 extracted fields spanning trace topology (`trace_id`, `span_id`, `parent_span_id`, `span_type`, `name`), model metadata (`model_name`, `model_provider`, `workflow_name`), status/errors (`status`, `error_type`, `is_error`, `error_message`), cost/latency (`duration_ms`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`), and RAG (`vector_store`, `embedding_model`, `documents_retrieved`, `relevance_score`, `prompt_text`, `response_text`).
  • 9 calculated fields, all Eval-based (no Lookup-type calculations) so the model stays fully acceleratable via `tstats`: `is_error_any`, `total_tokens`, `tokens_per_sec`, `ttft_estimate`, `latency_bucket`, `token_bucket`, and per-stage `retrieval_latency` / `generation_latency` / `embedding_latency`.
  • 5 child objects for clean drill-down: `LLM_Calls` (`span_type=LLM`), `Retrievals` (`RETRIEVER`), `Agents` (`AGENT`), `Tools` (`TOOL`), and `Errors` (`is_error=1`).
  • Acceleration ships OFF for Splunk Cloud / Splunkbase compliance. Summary config is pre-tuned (30-day range, 7-day backfill, 10-minute refresh) and ready to enable from Settings → Data Models. Dashboards run `summariesonly=false allow_old_summaries=true`, so they return correct results before acceleration is turned on and transparently use summaries once it is.

Alerts / Saved Searches (4 new, shipped enabled)

Four out-of-the-box correlation alerts. Each is gated by a volume or cost floor, so it ships enabled (`disabled = 0`) but stays silent until real traffic flows. All use digest mode, alert tracking, and per-alert suppression. Numeric thresholds are marked TUNE in each description and can be promoted to `macros.conf` for central tuning.

  • GenAI – Error rate above threshold by workflow (severity 5) — fires when LLM error rate for a workflow exceeds 5% over 15 min with at least 20 requests. Runs every 15 min; suppresses 30 min.
  • GenAI – Cost spike by model and workflow (severity 4) — fires when an hour's spend for a model+workflow exceeds 3× its trailing 24h hourly average, with a $1 floor. Runs hourly; suppresses 1h.
  • GenAI – P95 latency SLO breach (severity 4) — fires when P95 LLM latency for a model+workflow exceeds 8000 ms over 15 min with at least 20 requests. Runs every 15 min; suppresses 30 min.
  • GenAI – Token budget burn (projected daily) (severity 3) — projects end-of-day token usage from the elapsed fraction of the day and fires when the projection exceeds the daily budget (default 10,000,000 tokens). Runs hourly; suppresses 6h.

Alerts reference the shared search macros (`genai_llm_spans`, `genai_traces_index`, `genai_cost_lookup`, `genai_calculate_cost`), so cost and span-selection logic stays consistent with the dashboards.


Short Description:
Observability for LLM, RAG & agent apps. Works with any OpenTelemetry GenAI pipeline — no custom SDK required. Pre-built Splunk dashboards for tokens, latency, cost & errors.


Description:
GenAI Observability for Splunk provides production monitoring for LLM, RAG, and agent applications — track token usage, latency, cost, retrieval quality, and errors across OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, and more. **Works with any OpenTelemetry GenAI pipeline — no custom SDK required.** If you already emit OpenTelemetry GenAI traces (gen_ai.* semantic conventions), point your OpenTelemetry Collector at Splunk and the dashboards light up — with no changes to your application code. Prefer a turnkey setup? An optional lightweight Python SDK instruments your code with simple decorators. Key Features: - Ingests standard OpenTelemetry GenAI traces (gen_ai.* semantic conventions) via the OpenTelemetry Collector - Real-time monitoring of LLM calls, RAG pipelines, and AI agents - Token usage tracking with cost estimation (bundled model-pricing lookup) - Latency analysis with P50, P95, P99 percentiles and tokens/sec - Error detection and alerting - Pre-built dashboards for immediate insights - Optional Python SDK for one-line, decorator-based instrumentation - Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and any OpenTelemetry-instrumented framework - Data model acceleration to speed up reporting and dashboard performance on extremely large datasets Use Cases: - Monitor production AI applications - Optimize token usage and reduce costs - Debug slow or failing LLM calls - Track AI spend by model, workflow, or user - Ensure SLA compliance for AI services Bring your existing OpenTelemetry pipeline, or use the optional SDK — either way you get ready-to-use dashboards, model-pricing lookups, and a collector recipe to get started in minutes. The Splunk App for the Cybersecurity Extension for SAP (CES) enables security operations teams to monitor, investigate, and respond to SAP security threats directly within Splunk. Integrating SAP security logs with Splunk is challenging due to the complexity of multiple SAP log sources, inconsistent log formats, high raw data volumes, and the lack of predefined SAP-specific detection rules in Splunk. The CES Splunk app addresses these challenges by providing a purpose-built integration that filters, normalises, enriches, and forwards SAP security events to Splunk in real time. The app provides preconfigured dashboards covering three security domains: Alerts, Vulnerabilities, and Security Notes. Alerts are based on more than 1,200 out-of-the-box threat detection patterns applied by CES across SAP systems. Vulnerabilities represent system and user-related security weaknesses detected by CES through daily automated scans using a library of 3,000+ SAP-related checks. Security Notes track relevant, unapplied SAP security patches and their implementation status across systems. Status changes for alerts, vulnerabilities, and security notes are synchronised between CES and Splunk at configurable intervals, ensuring results remain current. Results can be filtered by date, time, system, environment, priority, and status. The app supports deployment via Splunk Universal Forwarder or Syslog and is compatible with Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud.

item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

The 5.1.1 release fixes a UI issue where dashboard table entries would flicker at specific window resolutions

The 5.1.0 release is a UI refresh focused on the Configure Lookup and Configure Suppressions dashboards. Alerting and suppression semantics are unchanged.

What's New

  • Faster dashboards at scale
  • The configuration tables stay responsive when your `expectedTime` collection holds tens of thousands of rows. Scrolling, sorting, and filtering work smoothly at 25,000+ entries.
  • Smart Index / Sourcetype / Host inputs
  • When adding or editing entries, these fields now autocomplete against your environment's actual values. Type two or more characters to see matches; free-text values that don't appear in the dropdown are still accepted.
  • Cleaner batch entry layout
  • "Add Multiple Entries" lays each row's fields out vertically so long index/sourcetype/host names no longer scrunch.
  • Refreshed look
  • Dashboards use the current generation of Splunk's UI components for a more consistent look with modern Splunk Enterprise / Cloud.

Fixed

  • The Configure Lookup table search filter now broadens results when you correct a typo, instead of narrowing further from the previous match.
  • The "Populate with Default Values" button no longer appears when a search filters the table to zero matches. It only appears when the underlying collection is genuinely empty.
  • Edits, additions, and deletions are immediately visible to subsequent searches without a page refresh.

Note on first install

The Index / Sourcetype / Host autocomplete reads from three lookups populated by scheduled searches that run every four hours (`Lookup Gen - bh_host_cache`, `Lookup Gen - bh_index_cache`, `Lookup Gen - bh_sourcetype_cache`). On a brand-new install the autocomplete dropdowns will be empty until the first scheduled run completes. A Splunk admin can run any of these searches manually to populate the caches immediately.

Upgrading from 5.0.x

No data migration or configuration changes are required. Install the new version through Splunkbase or by reloading the app; the new dashboards take effect immediately.


Description:
Please review the documentation if upgrading to Broken Hosts 5.0.0+ from a 4.x.x version. The Broken Hosts App for Splunk is a useful tool for monitoring data going into Splunk. It has the ability to alert when hosts stop sending data into Splunk, as well as inspect the last time the final combination of data was received by Splunk. If the arrival of the final log for the index/sourcetype/host combination is later than expected, the Broken Hosts App will send an alert. This allows for quick status detection of the hosts and fast issue resolution. The Broken Hosts App for Splunk is the app for monitoring missing data in Splunk. The app’s three main objectives include: 1. Alerting when data is missing from Splunk in order to determine the cause. 2. Utilizing saved searches to facilitate rapid detection of the missing data. 3. Creating dashboards for visualization to help with further investigations. * Latest documentation can be found here: https://brokenhosts.hurricanelabs.com
